events.title: Detecting and Patching Log4j (Log4Shell): A Practical Playbook
events.summary: A community-published playbook explains how defenders can detect and patch Log4j (Log4Shell), using the vulnerability as a template for understanding how a logging library can become a remote code execution vector. It recounts the mechanism: a logged attacker-controlled string could trigger a JNDI lookup and make the application connect to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
events.why_it_matters: Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) is rated critical with a CVSS of 10.0, is listed in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerability catalogue, and has an EPSS score near the maximum, indicating extremely high exploitation likelihood. The record notes it remains a reference point for intrusion analysis more than four years after disclosure. Defenders can use the playbook as a model for building detection guidance against similar library-level RCE flaws.

claims.text: CISA lists CVE-2021-44228 as exploited in the wild, added 2021-12-10, with US federal agencies due to fix it by 2021-12-24.
CVE-2021-44228 is rated 10.0 (critical) under CVSS 3.1 by CISA in the CVE record.
FIRST's EPSS puts the chance of CVE-2021-44228 being exploited in the next 30 days at 100%.
A fix for org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-core (Maven) is published in 2.15.0, 2.3.1 and 2.12.2, per GHSA-jfh8-c2jp-5v3q.
A fix for org.ops4j.pax.logging:pax-logging-log4j2 (Maven) is published in 1.9.2, 1.10.8, 1.11.10 and 2.0.11, per GHSA-jfh8-c2jp-5v3q.
